checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is every log address in a receipt added to the bloom filter exactly once via add_to_bloom?

reachability.notes: Attacker-crafted transactions produce logs with specific addresses. If any address is skipped in bloom computation, the bloom differs across clients.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all code paths that process transaction receipts and compute bloom filters. 2. Trace the log address extraction logic from receipt processing through add_to_bloom calls. 3. Verify that every log entry's address field is passed to add_to_bloom exactly once. 4. Craft test transactions that produce multiple logs with distinct addresses and verify all addresses appear in the bloom filter. 5. Test edge cases: empty logs, logs with duplicate addresses, maximum number of logs per receipt. 6. Compare bloom filter output across different client implementations to detect divergence. 7. Attempt to construct a transaction that causes a log address to be skipped (e.g., through early returns, exception handling, or iteration bugs).
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0035, Trust Boundary: tb-008, Invariant: SG-002-bloom/INV-002. Missing a log address causes receipt root divergence and consensus split. PoC must demonstrate a log address being skipped in bloom computation.

checklist.title: Verify Execution Engine Log Processing: Does the execution engine correctly iterate over all logs when computing bloom filters?

reachability.notes: Attacker-crafted transactions produce logs with specific addresses. If any address is skipped in bloom computation, the bloom differs across clients.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review the execution engine's log iteration code for off-by-one errors or premature loop termination. 2. Verify that the log collection is fully iterated without any early breaks or continues that could skip entries. 3. Check error handling paths to ensure exceptions don't cause log addresses to be skipped. 4. Verify that nested logs (if applicable) are properly flattened before bloom computation. 5. Test with transactions that generate logs at iteration boundaries (first log, last log, empty log list). 6. Ensure idempotency: while adding twice has no functional effect due to OR operation, detect any logic paths that would add twice as they indicate potential bugs in iteration logic.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0035, Supporting check for actor-execution-engine. Adding a log address twice indicates a logic error in iteration even though OR is idempotent.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are all log topics added to the bloom filter exactly once via add_to_bloom?

reachability.notes: Attacker-crafted transactions produce logs with specific topics. If any topic is skipped, the bloom differs across clients.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the add_to_bloom function and all call sites within log processing code. 2. Trace the loop that iterates over log.topics and verify each topic triggers exactly one add_to_bloom call. 3. Verify the log address is also added (total calls should be 1 + len(log.topics)). 4. Craft test transactions that produce logs with edge cases: zero topics, maximum topics, duplicate topics. 5. Compare the computed bloom filter against reference implementations. 6. Verify no early returns or error paths skip topic processing. 7. Check for off-by-one errors in loop bounds or array indexing.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0036, Source Invariant: SG-002-bloom/INV-003, Trust Boundary: tb-008. Attacker-controlled transaction logs can cause consensus splits if bloom filter computation differs between clients.

checklist.title: Verify execution engine correctly processes log topics at trust boundary tb-008

reachability.notes: Attacker-crafted transactions produce logs with specific topics. If any topic is skipped, the bloom differs across clients.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review the actor-execution-engine node for log receipt handling. 2. Verify that log processing at boundary tb-008 validates all topics are present before bloom computation. 3. Check for any filtering or sanitization that could inadvertently drop topics. 4. Test with malformed log structures to ensure robust handling. 5. Verify consistent behavior across all code paths that process transaction receipts.
checklist.notes: Supporting node check for actor-execution-engine. Source: PROP-0036.

checklist.title: Falsify Post-Condition: Can logs_bloom return a Bloom filter constructed from a partially processed log state?

reachability.notes: A race condition or early return in logs_bloom could produce a bloom from partial log processing.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the logs_bloom function implementation and trace its complete execution flow from entry to return. 2. Map all code paths that can lead to early return before all logs are fully processed (including error handlers, exception catches, and conditional returns). 3. Analyze the bytearray mutation sequence to identify intermediate states where partial bloom could be observed. 4. Construct test cases with multiple logs containing multiple topics each to verify bloom is computed only after full processing completes. 5. Inject simulated race conditions, interrupts, or concurrent access patterns to attempt triggering early return or partial state exposure. 6. Compare the actual bloom output against expected bloom computed from the complete log set using reference implementation. 7. Verify that no intermediate bloom states are exposed, returned, or persisted during processing. 8. Check exception handling paths to ensure partial bloom is not returned on error conditions. 9. Verify the bytearray is fully mutated (all logs and all topics processed) before any return statement. 10. Test with logs that cause maximum processing time to expose potential timeout-related early returns.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0037, Source Invariant: SG-002-bloom/INV-004. Post-condition verification: The bloom must be constructed from the fully mutated bytearray after all logs and their topics have been processed. Partial bloom construction produces incorrect bloom values, causing receipt root divergence. PoC must demonstrate early return or incomplete processing in logs_bloom.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is receipt bloom filter consistency validated against logs before accepting P2P blocks?

reachability.notes: Attacker sends block with receipt containing a bloom that does not match the logs. If bloom consistency is not verified, incorrect blooms propagate.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the P2P block reception handler where receipts are processed (trust boundary tb-008). 2. Locate the bloom filter validation logic that computes compute_bloom(receipt.logs) and compares it to receipt.bloom. 3. Craft a malicious block containing a receipt where the bloom field is intentionally inconsistent with the logs array. 4. Submit this block via P2P network interface and verify it is rejected at the block validation layer. 5. Verify error handling properly rejects the block without propagating the invalid receipt. 6. Check that no partial state is persisted if validation fails mid-processing. 7. Test with various inconsistency patterns: completely wrong bloom, partially correct bloom, empty bloom with non-empty logs, non-empty bloom with empty logs.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0038, Trust Boundary: tb-008, Source Invariant: SG-007/INV-003. Bloom-to-logs consistency is critical for event filtering correctness and consensus integrity. Inconsistent blooms could cause incorrect event queries or consensus splits if bloom is included in receipt root calculation. PoC must demonstrate a receipt with bloom inconsistent with its logs being accepted.

checklist.title: Verify execution engine correctly computes bloom filters for locally generated receipts

reachability.notes: Attacker sends block with receipt containing a bloom that does not match the logs. If bloom consistency is not verified, incorrect blooms propagate.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the execution engine component (actor-execution-engine) responsible for generating receipts after transaction execution. 2. Verify the bloom filter computation algorithm correctly implements compute_bloom() over all logs in the receipt. 3. Create test transactions that generate various log patterns (empty logs, single log, multiple logs with different topics). 4. Verify the generated bloom filter correctly encodes all log addresses and topics. 5. Cross-validate by recomputing the bloom from stored logs and comparing to the stored bloom field. 6. Ensure the invariant compute_bloom(receipt.logs) == receipt.bloom holds for all locally generated receipts.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0038, Supporting node check for actor-execution-engine and actor-p2p-peer. Ensures internally generated receipts maintain bloom-logs consistency invariant.

filtered_properties.details: Property marked as bug_bounty_scope: out-of-scope. Log immutability is enforced internally with no external attack vector.
